meta.description: No — Dr. Seuss never wrote this. It appears in none of his books and is a modern, unsourced internet saying credited to him on social media.

answer.label: Not Dr. Seuss — an unsourced internet saying
answer.authorDates: Popularized online in the late 2000s – early 2010s; earliest author undocumented
answer.sourceLine: There is no evidence Dr. Seuss ever wrote or said this. The line appears in none of his books, verse, letters, or interviews, and no primary source has ever been produced. Wikiquote lists it under “Misattributed” ↗, saying only that it is “attributed to Dr. Seuss on social media,” and Goodreads files it as ‘attributed-no-source’ ↗. It is best treated as an anonymous modern saying, not a Seuss quotation.

source.heading: The paper trail

docMeta.dd: None — not found in any Dr. Seuss work

source.excerpt: You know you’re in love when you can’t fall asleep because reality is finally better than your dreams.
trail: Wikiquote ↗ places the line in its Misattributed section, annotated only “Attributed to Dr. Seuss on social media” — i.e. no work is cited.
The Wikiquote talk page ↗ records an editor flagging it as “another quote attributed to Dr. Seuss, without a source” before it was moved out of the sourced list.
On Goodreads ↗ the line has 127,000+ likes yet carries the tag attributed-no-source, underscoring that its popularity is not evidence of authorship.
A search of Quote Investigator returns no study tracing this wording to Dr. Seuss or to any earlier writer; no primary attestation has been located.
source.excerptNote: Circulated in this fixed form on quote-aggregator sites, image macros, and print-on-demand merchandise, nearly always credited to “Dr. Seuss” with no book, page, or date attached.
source.rightsNote: Because the wording’s true origin is undocumented — it is not tied to any Dr. Seuss work or to any other identified author or dated publication — no copyright status can be responsibly asserted. It should be treated as an anonymous modern saying of uncertain rights.

author.name: Dr. Seuss (Theodor Seuss Geisel)
author.heading: Why it gets pinned on Dr. Seuss
author.bio: Theodor Seuss Geisel (1904–1991), writing as Dr. Seuss, created The Cat in the Hat, Green Eggs and Ham, How the Grinch Stole Christmas! and Oh, the Places You’ll Go! His warm, rhyming, aphoristic voice makes him one of the internet’s biggest magnets for feel-good sayings he never wrote. This romantic one-liner has none of his rhyme or cadence and appears nowhere in his published work — it simply borrows his name for authority.

misattribution.heading: How the misattribution works
misattribution.intro: This is a textbook “famous-name feel-good” misattribution: a sentimental one-liner attached to a beloved author to lend it weight, with no citation ever provided.

items.why: The line does not appear in any Dr. Seuss book, poem, speech, or interview. Wikiquote lists it as misattributed ↗, noting only that it is “attributed to Dr. Seuss on social media,” and no primary source has ever surfaced.

misattribution.truthLine: No documented source connects this sentence to Dr. Seuss; it is best described as an anonymous, source-less internet saying ↗ that borrows his name.

context.heading: Why this one spreads
lead: The sentence is compact, romantic, and endlessly shareable — ideal for image macros, wedding readings, and greeting cards. Dr. Seuss’s name gives an anonymous line instant credibility, which is exactly why unsourced sayings gravitate to famous authors.

Notably, the wording carries none of Seuss’s signature rhyme or playful meter. That stylistic mismatch, plus the total absence of a book or date, is the tell that this is a modern saying wearing a borrowed name.
